subject: FinPilot demo request — intake: use case, traffic, timeline
messages:
From: Alexandra Wu <alex.wu@finpilot.io>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Demo request — FinPilot signup + quick context

Hi Lauren / Tessa,

We just signed up for Redwood (self-serve) and I wanted to see if we could schedule a short demo to understand how Redwood would fit our customer-facing assistant. A bit of context:

- Use case: customer-support assistant that surface personalized product recommendations + private KB answers (we host docs).
- Expected monthly usage: ~500k tokens/month during pilot (mostly generation + embeddings for search).
- Traffic shape: daily active users ~2–3k; peak concurrency around 40–60 users, occasional spikes up to ~200 QPS for short bursts.
- Timeline: pilot in ~4–6 weeks; production targeted Q3 if pilot looks good.

We'd like to confirm: 1) whether you have an async/streaming demo that covers batching and KV-cache behavior, and 2) how you'd recommend we size for the pilot. Happy to share a CSV export of sample traffic if helpful.

Timezone: PST (San Francisco). I’m available next Tue/Wed morning (PST) or Thu afternoon.

Thanks — Alex
Alexandra Wu
Head of Product, FinPilot
alex.wu@finpilot.io
+1 415-555-0183

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alexandra Wu <alex.wu@finpilot.io>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo request — FinPilot signup + quick context

Hi Alex — great to meet you, and welcome aboard.

Tessa and I can run a focused 30–45 minute session that covers: concise demo of streaming and KV caching, batching strategies for cost/latency tradeoffs, and sizing for pilot vs prod. Before we lock a slot, a couple quick clarifying questions so we tailor the call:  

1) Traffic detail: when you say "200 QPS spikes" — is that concurrent inference requests or aggregated token QPS? Do you expect those spikes to last minutes or hours?
2) Latency SLO: do you have a target p95 (e.g., <250ms) for customer-facing responses?
3) Embeddings: are you planning to precompute embeddings and store them, or compute on-the-fly for each query? Approx embeddings/month?
4) Security/compliance: do you require SOC2, enterprise SSO, or data residency (US-only/EU)?
5) Pilot success criteria: what metrics would make the pilot a go/no-go? (cost per 1k tokens, latency, answer quality, uptime)

If you can drop a small sample (CSV) with daily request counts and average tokens per request that will help us generate a sizing suggestion. I attached our short demo checklist so you can see what we’ll cover.

Proposed slots (PST):
- Thu 11 Jun 10:00–10:45
- Tue 16 Jun 09:00–09:45
- Wed 17 Jun 11:30–12:15

If none of those work, tell us a couple of windows and Ben (cc'd) can pick up calendar logistics.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-demo-checklist.pdf (1 page — agenda + pre-reqs)

From: Alexandra Wu <alex.wu@finpilot.io>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo request — FinPilot signup + quick context

Hi Lauren / Tessa,

Thanks — answers below inline. Happy to attach a small sample export; I’ve included two attachments: a short CSV and a one-page architecture overview.

1) The 200 QPS is concurrent inference requests (short spikes during batch runs) — typically minutes, sometimes up to 20 minutes when we push a campaign.
2) Latency target: p95 <= 300ms for text-generation responses (we can accept slightly higher for longer responses).
3) Embeddings: we'll precompute most embeddings and store them; expect ~150k embeddings/month during pilot.
4) Security: SOC2 is required for pilot access; SSO (Okta) is needed at production. Data residency: US-only for now.
5) Pilot success: 1) p95 under 350ms for typical queries; 2) predictable cost < $X per 1k tokens (we can discuss targets on call); 3) no blocking security issues.

Sample attachments: finpilot-traffic-export.csv (rows: timestamp,avg_tokens,requests) and architecture-overview.pdf (very small).

Preferred slot: Tue 16 Jun 09:00 PST works best. If you can send calendar invite, we’ll confirm.

Cheers,
Alex

Attachment: finpilot-traffic-export.csv
Attachment: architecture-overview.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alexandra Wu <alex.wu@finpilot.io>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo request — FinPilot signup + quick context

Hi Alex — thanks for the details and the files. I’ve sent a calendar invite for Tue 16 Jun 09:00–09:45 PST (30-minute demo + 15 for Q&A). Please accept when convenient.

Next steps for the meeting:
- Lauren/Tessa will demo streaming, caching, and proposed pilot configuration.
- We’ll review the sample traffic and suggest instance sizing + batching/quantization options.
- Post-call: we’ll follow up with a short pilot questionnaire (attached) and a DocuSign NDA link if you need one.

Links & attachments: Pilot questionnaire (pilot-questionnaire.xlsx), HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/FP-342), NDA (https://www.docusign.com/sign?doc=FP-NDA-2026).

If you’d like Lauren to invite an engineering lead from our side (runtime engineer) include a +1 on the accept. Looking forward to it.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
